articles.title: 'The Altruists' Review: Anthony Boyle and Julia Garner Make a Toxically Perfect Match in Netflix's Intriguing but Unsatisfying Crypto Love Story
articles.summary: Based on the real-life rise and fall of FTX, the eight-part miniseries from Graham Moore ('The Imitation Game') delves into the romance between founder Sam Bankman-Fried and exec Caroline Ellison.
articles.content:
As FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried ( Anthony Boyle ) begins his very public downfall, one salacious detail starts to go viral: That Caroline Ellison ( Julia Garner ), CEO of sister firm Alameda and his ex-girlfriend, was a prolific writer of smutty Harry Potter fanfiction.

The fact that her private hobby has nothing to do with the financial crimes they're in hot water for is beside the point. “What gets more clicks than a complicated financial scandal? A young professional woman who's into kink," shrugs Constance (Madison Hu), FTX’s loyal-to-the-end COO. "I mean, that's the story. The whole world didn't care about Caroline until they realized that she was horny.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Netflix's New Releases Coming in November 2026 TV 'The Altruists': Anthony Boyle's Sam Bankman-Fried Caught in Crypto Crisis in Netflix Series Trailer The Altruists The Bottom Line All heart and not enough head. Airdate: Thursday, Nov. 19 (Netflix) Cast: Julia Garner, Anthony Boyle, Alex Lawther, Karan Soni, Madison Hu, Eugene Young, Naomi Okada, Matt Rife, Robin Weigert, Paul Reiser, Terry Chen Creator: Graham Moore

Sam, who knows better than anyone how mortified Caroline must be, seems troubled by the notion. But it more or less appears to be the impulse driving Netflix’s The Altruists . The eight-hour series chronicles the rise and fall of FTX and Alameda through the tumultuous relationship between its leaders — and in doing so, deepens the saga's emotional relatability while also diminishing its stakes.

For most of the season, creator Graham Moore ( The Imitation Game ) cuts between two timelines. In the halcyon days of 2016, captured by director James Ponsoldt in the warm bright tones and slightly grainy texture of an indie rom-com, Caroline meets Sam on her first day at a New York hedge fund. The two recognize each other almost immediately as kindred spirits, matched in their intelligence (high), their interests (math and winning) and their taste in jokes (charmingly dorky).

In no time, they’re falling into bed, though not quite into a relationship — Caroline prefers to keep it caszh, reasoning that non-monogamy is more “mathematically optimal” for getting off. Instead, they tie their fates together via their careers. Sam first founds Alameda and then FTX, and in short order brings Caroline on board as an exec. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The businesses are rooted in the couple's shared principle of effective altruism. In theory, EA is a rationalist moral framework that prioritizes doing the greatest good. In practice, like most guiding philosophies, it's easily twisted into whatever a self-interested devotee wants it to be.

Betraying a colleague, conning oblivious business partners, stealing customer money — why, any of it might be justifiable, noble even, so long as it's done with the intention of making more money to definitely for sure donate to some worthy cause someday. And so it is that in the show’s other, grayer timeline, it’s 2022 and Sam and Caroline find themselves scrambling to cover up all the grave financial misdeeds they've committed in service of some vague higher purpose.

How one timeline could lead into the other is The Altruists ’ central concern, though the answer isn't really much mystery (and not only because it was all headline news a scant four years ago). The differences between the Caroline and Sam we meet in 2016 and the ones we’ll part with in 2022 are ones of degree, not kind. These two have always been aggressive about taking risks, arrogant about their ability to outplay them, skeptical of the rules and gifted in justifying their own bullshit to themselves as perfectly rational, and therefore objectively correct, decisions.

Add in the fact that they tend to augment each other’s worst impulses — backing each other’s wildest moves, one-upping each other for spite or for fun, treating every office disagreement like a proxy for the conversations about commitment or exclusivity they’re supposedly too evolved to need — and FTX/Alameda’s meltdown starts to look almost inevitable. As ex-colleague and ex-friend Trabucco (a very good Alex Lawther) puts it, “Sam was a block of sodium. Caroline was a rushing river.” Put those ingredients together, the MIT graduate explains, and you’ve got an instant fireball. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

If the journey contains few surprises, however, it does offer some worthy features. Karan Soni brings much-needed sweetness as FTX engineer Nishad, whose cute will-they-won't-they with a coworker (Naomi Okada) becomes collateral damage in the implosion. Paul Reiser and Robin Weigert are fun in supporting roles as Sam’s parents, though their appearances are so brief that another character has to explain that while they love their son, they don’t like him. On the other end of the lovability spectrum, Terry Chen drinks up the part of possibly mob-affiliated rival crypto founder CZ with as much gusto as his character does his fancy health tonics.

The real (vegan) meat of the story, of course, is the bond between Sam and Caroline. That, the series understands inside and out. Boyle disappears into the part of Sam, whose boyish arrogance is somehow both his most alluring quality and his most repugnant. He's outdone only slightly by the chameleonic Garner, who plays the mousy but mighty Caroline like she might see all the gears turning just underneath the surface of reality if she only stares hard enough.

When the two are across a room from one another, even editing a spreadsheet can turn into an act of thrilling flirtation. I hesitate to describe their chemistry as irresistible only because that might suggest we want to see them together. In actuality, the questionably effective but not entirely unpleasant experience of watching The Altruists is to simultaneously believe with your whole heart that these crazy kids are meant for each other and that we'd all have been better off if they'd never met. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The show’s intense focus on their love story distinguishes it, somewhat, from the increasingly crowded field of dramas about scammy and scummy tech founders. The usual rise-fall arc is emotionally complicated by the ménage à trois between Sam, Caroline and FTX/Alameda: The lovers might insist they always put the work first, but The Altruists know well how vulnerable even billionaire geniuses can be to whims of their hearts or loins. ( Ahem. )

But as a way into what is still ultimately the story of a tech scam, the romantic angle doesn't entirely work. Amid all the whirlwind drama, a sense of perspective gets lost. The number $8 billion, as in the amount of money FTX has stolen from its customers, gets lobbed about in every episode. But who those clients are, what impact the crime has in the larger world, what cultural forces allowed SBF's FTX to get so big so fast to begin with, what consequences are left in the wake of its collapse — all these factors are barely mentioned at all.

You come away with the sense that the real lesson of the whole FTX debacle is what a tragedy it is when two people so intelligent are too caught up in their own heads to simply say what's in their hearts, to the point that it's easier to perpetrate financial crimes on a historic scale than it is to simply say "I love you." In a vacuum, I suppose it's a worthy lesson. In a broader context, however, it seems an unreasonably expensive one.

articles.title: 'The Altruists' Review: Netflix FTX Series Fails to Get a Handle on Crypto Scammer Sam Bankman-Fried
articles.summary: The collapse of cryptocurrency exchange FTX in 2022 — a spectacular implosion that saw the company evaporate and sent founder Sam Bankman-Fried to prison, along with much of his inner circle — felt epic in the moment. But compared to the frenzy around artificial intelligence that was soon to come, even the Shakespearean downfall of […]
articles.content:
The collapse of cryptocurrency exchange FTX in 2022 — a spectacular implosion that saw the company evaporate and sent founder Sam Bankman-Fried to prison, along with much of his inner circle — felt epic in the moment. But compared to the frenzy around artificial intelligence that was soon to come, even the Shakespearean downfall of a corporation that could once casually spend nine figures on stadium naming rights feels like a footnote in the intertwined history of technology and finance. The crypto boom now occupies an awkward middle space in the recent arc of the tech industry: After the Obama-era idealism of Facebook, Twitter and other companies that promised to connect the world for the better and before the full-on dystopian rhetoric of post-human labor and a “permanent underclass.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Darren Aronofsky's Protozoa and Memory to Adapt Chris Miller's 'Chip War' into Feature Documentary (EXCLUSIVE) Elon Musk Has Invested in Skydance, David Ellison Confirms: 'To Have Him as a Shareholder Is an Honor'

The Netflix limited series “ The Altruists ,” created by Graham Moore (the Oscar-winning screenwriter of “The Imitation Game”) and produced by the Obamas’ shingle Higher Ground, is aware of this gap. “AI is hotter than crypto’s ever been right now,” one character observes in the finale as FTX’s house of cards starts to fall. (Marquee frontier lab and FTX investee Anthropic even makes a cameo.) “The Altruists” could theoretically use our rapidly fading cultural memory to its advantage, dusting off the Bankman-Fried story to deliver a character study that pushes past tabloid headlines about polycules and party mansions to make sense of what happened and a case for why it mattered.

Instead, “The Altruists” opts for the most conventional, least persuasive lens through which to explain the significance of FTX as well as what went wrong: the on-and-off romance between Bankman-Fried (Irish actor Anthony Boyle) and Caroline Ellison (Julia Garner, also an executive producer), the former head of FTX-affiliated hedge fund Alameda Research. The action toggles back and forth between two timelines: the early days of Sam, Caroline and their companies and their swift demise five years later, forecasted in a standard flash-forward to the FBI storming the office. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The erstwhile couple make a certain sense as the show’s focus. They’re a handy metaphor for the messy, inappropriate relationship between their two companies, which culminated in FTX’s use of billions in customer money to cover for Alameda’s trading losses. And, of course, there are salacious details like Ellison’s X-rated “Harry Potter” fanfiction — the kind of low-hanging fruit a writer would have to be foolish to leave on the vine. Sex still sells, even when the sex in question is between socially awkward math geeks whose idea of foreplay is strategic board games.

But “The Altruists,” which works from a series of New York magazine articles by Kevin T. Dugan and Jen Wieczner as its source material, makes Sam and Caroline strangely simplistic, both as individual personalities and larger cultural forces. It starts with the casting: Boyle is a strong actor with a bright future ahead of him; the onetime face of a brash IRA revolutionary in "Say Nothing" is nonetheless an awkward fit for a noted oddball like Bankman-Fried, and Boyle never disappears into the role. His SBF — the boy billionaire’s popular nickname — is motormouthed and visibly anxious, yet the scripts elide some of his strangest tics, like taking interviews while playing video games or sleeping on the office floor. (The bean bag habit is alluded to in dialogue, yet never shown. An odd choice for a visual medium!) Boyle’s performance comes off more like the Mark Zuckerberg of “The Social Network,” a disaffected yet basically relatable nerd who craves validation, than the Mark Zuckerberg of “The Social Reckoning,” a space alien whose inability to grasp human nature has warped the world in his image.

Garner, for her part, dials up Ellison’s tics into a near-caricature of a four-eyed poindexter. Pre-arrest footage of Ellison, who would go on to cooperate extensively with SBF’s prosecutors, shows the same nervous laughter that Garner accurately mimics, but a much more calm and even speaking voice. Amping up an accent and donning a wig are old hat for the star of “Inventing Anna,” another frustrating Netflix project that captured its subject’s eccentricity without delving into their deeper psychology. Were “The Altruists” more of a straight-up satire in tone, Garner’s caricature might work in context. Instead, isolated moments of humor — upon finding out about the fraud, one FTX employee is mad because he's been urging them to break the law for years and feels excluded — are left to float in an otherwise sincere story of misguided puppy love. (In a striking detail seemingly invented for the show, Caroline is the first woman Sam ever sleeps with.) Perhaps Moore and co-showrunner Jacqueline Hoyt were worried about crossing over into gleeful cruelty. But if perpetrators of a multibillion dollar fraud don’t deserve some mockery, who does? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Sam and Caroline are initially drawn together as young analysts at the Wall Street firm Jane Street Capital by their mutual interest in effective altruism, the “earn to give” movement that gives “The Altruists” its name. (Characters affiliated with EA are frequently identified by their branded T-shirts.) The two encourage each other’s most dangerous instincts, like going all in on every bet because it’s “mathematically optimal” or refusing to communicate discomfort around Sam’s autocratic tendencies or Caroline’s polyamory. The plot frames Sam and Caroline’s slide into criminality as the slow corruption of self-identified “good guys,” though the show is strangely uncritical of the starting premise that the best way to make positive change in the world is by amassing a personal fortune.

For all EA comes into focus, cryptocurrency itself remains stubbornly obscure. It’s not easy to mine drama from complex financial instruments, but “The Altruists” puts frustratingly little effort into explaining the water these crazy kids are swimming in. Without a more defined sense of what makes crypto unique, “The Altruists” is left with a faint rehash of the techno-optimism-gone-awry narrative already explored in series like “The Dropout,” “Super Pumped” and “WeCrashed,” which tellingly dropped within weeks of each other in 2022 (and just a few months before FTX flamed out). Those three titles collectively worked to capture a specific time and place; with its personal focus, “The Altruists” never does the same.

“The Altruists” even gestures at more productive angles on the whole FTX affair than the folie a deux of Sam and Caroline. Potential framing devices, like a Bloomberg reporter’s investigation, are flirted with and abandoned. Nishad Singh (Karan Soni), SBF’s childhood friend turned employee, tells us that Sam’s Stanford Law professor parents Joe (Paul Reiser) and Barbara (Robin Weigert) are the skeleton key to his need to prove himself. “They already love you,” Nishad says of the scholars. “They just don’t fucking like you.” It’s a great line, just not one backed up in any way by the show’s portrayal of that relationship, which is fairly minimal and fails to lay the groundwork for head-scratching decisions like Joe and Barbara’s total credulity toward their son, both before and after his arrest. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It’s not like “The Altruists” lacks time to explore the Bankman-Fried household dynamics. (The resources to convincingly render far-flung locations like Macau and Malta do, however, seem scarce.) At eight hourlong episodes, “The Altruists” is padded out with detours into Nishad’s office romance and the backstory of SBF’s college pal Sam Trabucco (Alex Lawther), who left FTX before things hit the fan. The space would be far better spent building out the crypto universe, shading in Sam and Caroline outside one another’s orbit or even outlandish incidents like FTX’s Larry David-starring Super Bowl ad. Without a stronger center, though, these satellite plots feel like they’re orbiting a vacuum.

All eight episodes of “The Altruists” are now streaming on Netflix.

articles.content:
Hearst Canvas , the creator-led media arm of U.K.-based Hearst Networks, has launched its latest digital native brand with Frontier Collective , an effort to harness the YouTube and social media followings of top outdoor adventure content creators.

The effort has quietly bowed over the past few weeks starting with a roundtable-style talk show, “Expedition HQ,” featuring four prominent U.K. explorers at the core of Frontier Collective: Aldo Kane, Alex Bescoby, Levison Wood and Lucy Shepherd. The foursome come together swap stories about explorations and derring-do in their efforts to explore the natural world and far-flung exotic locales. “Expedition HQ” bowed Nov. 1 on the Frontier Collective YouTube channel, with new episodes released weekly. Clips are spread widely around Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and Snapchat. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Jamie Dornan Hasn’t ‘Spoken Directly’ to Viggo Mortensen About Aragorn Recasting in ‘Lord of the Rings: Hunt for Gollum,’ But Says ‘His Approval’ is ‘All I Care About’ Robert Pattinson Trolled by U.K. Government in Youth Employment Scheme Post After Bond Reveal: He’ll ‘Apply for All 90,000 Jobs’

Hearst Canvas hopes to tap into the heat of the adventure content community on YouTube. The Hearst Canvas division is set up to find top-tier creators who can contribute to strong verticals as Hearst Networks develops new content and formats designed to roll out on YouTube. Dean Possenniskie, managing director, Hearst Networks, Europe, Middle East and Africa and managing director Hearst Networks U.K., is overseeing the Canvas venture that was launched in October 2025.

“We’ve now built a dedicated creative team that is going to originate formats in a different style that are designed to work as creator-led content on YouTube,” Possenniskie told Variety . “A format like Frontier Collective is unique in the fact it brings together four very strong talents in the space. It’s not an audience that we traditionally reach here in the U.K. through pay TV or DTC or broadcast channels. It’s a global audience, and it’s a much broader audience for us to reach now as well. So that’s a really exciting opportunity.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Hearst Canvas is headed by Danny Baggot as creative director and Sam Pearson as executive producer. The pair unveiled the venture’s first commission on Oct. 29, the unscripted business revitalization series “Pitch, Please."

“Frontier Collective offers a compelling opportunity to build something unique in the adventure space — a network of remarkable individuals whose passion drives them to explore the far reaches of our globe and share what they’ve experienced with the world,” Pearson said. “And with 'Expedition HQ,' we’re launching a returning format that delivers on this promise through fascinating and insightful conversations.”

The roundtable series is produced by Grammar Productions, co-founded by Bescoby. It’s produced shows for BBC, Channel 4, Apple TV, Amazon Prime, Discovery, Sky HISTORY and Canal+, in addition to custom work for brands.

As a veteran of the adventure genre, Bescoby said he sees demand for Frontier Collective as a concept.

“Some of the best adventure storytellers I know have spent years asking for a proper home for their work,” Bescoby said. “Traditional television has stepped back from the genre, even as audiences are clamoring for more. It’s hugely exciting that Hearst Canvas is building that home with Frontier Collective, and it’s amazing to be a part of it."

Kane invoked the importance of the YouTube channel as serving as a hub for adventure content fan communities. “This new YouTube channel allows us to bring directly to our community the real story that goes on behind the scenes on these adventures,” he said.

Wood added that every major adventure yields its own unique experiences, and inevitably, there is more color than can be included in the final program. “So much never makes it into the finished documentaries. I’m looking forward to sharing more of those experiences and unseen footage on my own channels as part of Frontier Collective,” Wood said.

Shepherd added her enthusiasm for the push to build a hub for top digital-native explorers and adventurers.

“I’m only sorry this didn’t begin sooner. There’s something very special about sitting around a table with people whose adventures inspired me to set out on my own,” Shepherd said. “Life is an expedition, and I hope our stories inspire others to find a little adventure in their lives, wherever they are.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Argentinian Spanish actor and director Botto is a celebrated actor with close to 80 features to his name, with recent credits including The Suicide Squad , The Room Next Door and Breaking Falls . His feature directorial debut On The Fringe premiered in the Venice Film Festival’s Horizons sidebar in 2022.

"After two years of writing and a long research process, which included hours of interviews with women who trusted us with their stories, it is a privilege for me to tell this story with this cast and this creative team,” he said.

Netflix launched in Spain in 2015, where it has since established its biggest European production hub dedicated to non-English-language production. articles.content:
Wicker ' s filmmaking team is relishing its viral moments and box office success — not to mention its horny memes .

During a screening of Wicker at Toruń Camerimage Film Festival in Poland on Thursday, cinematographer Lol Crawley introduced the movie and expressed appreciation for it having become a social media sensation. Olivia Colman stars in directors Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer's romantic fantasy as a lonely woman who commissions a basket weaver (Peter Dinklage) to create a husband ( Alexander Skarsgard ) for her. "It's my fourth time back at the festival and having the honor of screening a film in competition, so thank you so much to Camerimage," Crawley said from the stage about the festival that honors cinematography . Later, after a festival representative had finished translating Crawley's speech into Polish for the crowd, the Wicker cinematographer quipped, "Now I know what 'wicker nipples' is in Polish, which is a takeaway for me."

articles.title: Indigenous Queer Drama 'Princess' Is Dedicated to "Everyone Fighting for Their Freedom, Their Identity"
articles.summary: Ecuadorian writer-director Christian Rojas' feature debut, which just premiered at Tallinn, is a contribution to the collective healing of wounds, both the creative's own and other people's.
articles.content:
Princess , or Ñusta in the Andean indigenous language Quechua, is not your standard coming-of-age film. At the heart of Ecuadorian writer-director Christian Rojas' lyrical debut feature is Kallpa, 12, who has a big dream: to be chosen as Ñusta, the princess in the teenager's Andean community’s Winter Solstice Festival. But having been born in the body of a boy, Kallpa is barred from taking part. Rigid tradition and community rejection mean that Kallpa must find a new home and family among a group of local trans women.

Kuri Fuerez stars alongside La Bruja de Texcoco, Bruno Giganti, Quispe Nuna, Romel Vargas, Kayita Quizhpe and Adele Pesantez. Princess , which is a co-production between Ecuador, Mexico, Argentina, Peru and Bolivia, features cinematography by Christian Hidalgo and editing by Jorge Macaya and Cristian Bermeo. The producers are María Ángeles Palacios and Daniela Fuentes Moncada. Princess , featuring dialogue in Spanish and Quechua, just celebrated its world premiere in the First Feature Competition of the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF) in Estonia.

After the premiere screening, Rojas and members of the production and creative team discussed Princess with the audience.

" Ñusta was born when I was 10 years old, after I had experienced sexual abuse that [affected] my childhood and my life for a long time," Rojas shared. "I dedicate this film to those who have survived, to those who are still fighting, and to those who open their eyes every day [with] the strength to keep on [being] who they are – everyone fighting for their freedom, their identity, and their right to a life without fear." Rojas lauded his collaborators as "the best team I could ever have," concluding: "I say thank you to everyone for being part of it, part of healing this wound collectively – and not just my wound, but those wounds of everyone who's still fighting and thinks they're alone. We have to resist, raise our voice, and hug each other as a family." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Safeguarding and ensuring a safe space, especially for the young actors, was a core focus for the Princess team. "The indigenous families … knew the story from beginning to end, but not the children," Rojas said. "We had a psychologist on set and in pre-production, trying to develop this secure place for everyone so that we could actually enjoy making this movie."

And the writer-director shared: "It was important to me for the children to feel like it was a game that they were playing, and that it was not a rigid process. So with this amazing team, what we did was play and go through it by playing." One of the elements they used in the creative process with the kids was "a map of emotions," Rojas said.

The Princess team also emphasized the importance of working in and with the local community with respect. "We didn't want to extract anything," the director emphasized. "What we wanted was real participation and reciprocity."

The film team also included members of different indigenous communities, including some leaders within those communities who work on diversity and related issues.

The movie, set in 1997, includes an infamous real-life event that scarred Ecuador’s queer community that year. Police in the city of Cuenca back then raided a trans beauty pageant and arrested several people, who were then exposed to abuse and violence in custody. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"In terms of the visuals, we wanted to create the universe where Kallpa could travel, because this is a journey, and we wanted to always be with Kallpa on his journey," Hidalgo explained. "And second, we wanted to be very close, so we are always with Kallpa."

The sound also plays into Princess ' aesthetic of closeness, allowing the audience to hear things we cannot see from a distance.

When it came time to screen Princess for the community, "I was really afraid," Rojas shared. But he felt validated when "a 70-year-old lady stood up and said, 'We need to talk about these stories here in our community.'"

The company has recreated the Raichand family mansion from the 2001 film for a limited-time immersive experience in Mumbai , inviting fans to explore its grand staircase, family study and Poo's extravagant closet. The experience is being presented by Johar alongside Hrithik Roshan and Kareena Kapoor Khan, who played Rohan Raichand and Poo, respectively, in the film. The three stars will not appear in person

Released in December 2001, "Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham," commonly known as "K3G," featured an ensemble cast including Amitabh Bachchan, Jaya Bachchan, Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol. The family drama, which follows a wealthy Indian family divided by a son's marriage against his father's wishes, became one of the defining Bollywood films of its era, with its elaborate production design, musical numbers and fashion continuing to resonate with younger audiences.

The Airbnb recreation will allow guests to explore the mansion through an immersive audio tour featuring memorable moments from the film. Visitors can also step inside a recreation of Poo's wardrobe, participate in a character-inspired entry challenge and write a personal note inspired by the movie's themes of love and family. Each guest will receive a commemorative keepsake.

"Poo has been a part of my life for 25 years, and I love that she's still having her moment with a whole new generation," Kapoor Khan said in a statement. Roshan, meanwhile, described the experience as an opportunity to revisit one of his earliest major film roles.

"To see the Raichand House recreated by Airbnb and to know that fans will get to walk down the memory lane themselves is the best way to celebrate the film," he said.

The activation is part of Airbnb's "Only on Airbnb" experiences, which have increasingly tapped into entertainment properties and fan culture to create real-world versions of fictional settings.

Booking requests open Nov. 23 at 12 p.m. IST through Airbnb's dedicated K3G page. The experience is free, with each booking covering two guests, although visitors must arrange their own travel to Mumbai.

articles.content:
Suzanne Collins gave her readers a huge gift in returning to the world of The Hunger Games series, the first three books of which she wrote in 2008, 2009 and 2010, for the prequel story of one Haymitch Abernathy.

Haymitch, portrayed by Woody Harrelson in the quartet of films based on Collins’ original book trilogy, was Katniss Everdeen’s (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark’s (Josh Hutcherson) mentor for their two Hunger Games — the 74 th and 75 th .

For everything we know about the film adaptation of Hunger Game: Sunrise on the Reaping , read on:

When does the The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping film come out? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

The film will arrive in theaters November 20, 2026.

Will there be contemporary songs written for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ?

Yes, Noah Kahan announced that he has written "Draw You Out" as the lead single for the companion album to the film. The whole album, which features songs from Noah Cyrus, Ella Langley, Lizzy McAlpine, Smashing Pumpkins, Gigi Perez and more, arrived a week before the film hits theaters.

Is there a trailer for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ?

A fuller trailer showing new actors and actresses portraying younger versions of familiar characters arrived in April 2026, and still another one that hints at some of the more gruesome scenes from the novel arrived mid-September ahead of release this year.

Lionsgate released a teaser trailer Nov. 20, 2025 a year before the film will arrive in theaters. The clip features Close as Drusilla, Zada as Haymitch, Whitney Peak as Lenore Dove, McKenna Grace as Maysilee Donner, Ben Wang as Wyatt Callow, Jesse Plemons as Plutarch Heavensbee, Elle Fanning as Effie Trinket Ralph Fiennes as President Snow and more.

What sounds like Woody Harrelson's voiceover plays at the end of the clip, which follows the pattern of Donald Sutherland lending his voice to The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes , in which Tom Blyth portrayed a younger version of Sutherland's original President Snow.

Who will play Haymitch Abernathy in The Sunrise on the Reaping movie?

Joseph Zada has been cast in the main role of Haymitch for the film. Zada appeared in another highly anticipated book adaptation, the television series We Were Liars , Season 1 of which made a big splash on Prime Video in June. In that show, he plays Johnny Sinclair, and author E. Lockhart revealed that he will reprise the role in the recently renewed second season , which is based on Lockhart's prequel novel, Family of Liars .

Deadline exclusively reported Zada’s casting alongside the actress who will play Haymitch’s love interest, Lenore Dove Baird.

Who else is in the cast of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping film?

Whitney Peak will portray Lenore Dove Baird, Haymitch’s girl and a descendant of the Covey, the nomadic group of performers whom Collins expanded upon in her first prequel story, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes .

Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler), was a member of the Covey.

Deadline also exclusively broke the news of McKenna Grace’s casting as Maysilee Donner, another District 12 tribute, in the upcoming film.

Plutarch Heavensbee (portrayed by the late Philip Seymour-Hoffman in Catching Fire and Mockingjay Parts 1 and 2 ) will be played by Jesse Plemons, Deadline first reported .

Kelvin Harrison Jr. will portray Beetee Latier , who was originally played by Jeffrey Wright in Catching Fire and both parts of Mockingjay . Deadline exclusively reported that Maya Hawke has also joined the film as Wiress, originally portrayed by Amanda Plummer in Catching Fire and both parts of Mockingjay . Wiress won her Hunger Games in a mirrored arena, and she mentors the four District 12 tributes in Collins' book. Lili Taylor will portray Mags, formerly played by Lynn Cohen in Catching Fire (2013). Mags hails from District 4, and she also mentors the District 12 tributes in Haymitch's Hunger Games.

Lord Voldemort himself Ralph Fiennes will take on another big villain — President Snow — who was portrayed in the first four films by the late Donald Sutherland and in the prequel, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes about Snow's backstory, by Tom Blythe.

Ben Wang has been cast as Wyatt Callow, the other male tribute in the second Quarter Quell. Elle Fanning has been confirmed for the role of a younger Effie Trinket, portrayed by Elizabeth Banks in the original four films.

THR has exclusively reported that Molly McCann is set to play Louella, while Iona Bell will portray her Capitol-assigned lookalike Lou Lou.

Deadline broke the news that Glenn Close will play Drusilla Sickle, cold escort to the District 12 tributes and a sort of predecessor to Elizabeth Banks' Effie Trinket. Deadline also exclusively reported Billy Porter's casting as Magno Stift, Drusilla's estranged husband and the uninspired designer for District 12's tributes much like Lenny Kravitz's Cinna in the original trilogy of films. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

Deadline also first reported Jhaleil Swaby's casting as Panache, one of the arrogant and aggressive career tributes from District 1 in the second Quarter Quell.

What is The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping about?

The prequel story focuses on Haymitch’s Hunger Games. Obviously since he was around to mentor Katniss and Peeta in their first and (unfortunately) second set of games, he was a victor of his own games, but that did not make them any more gruesome, for his games were the 50 th set.

Every 25 years, the capitol of Panem, the dystopian nation in which these stories take place, reinforces what is called the Quarter Quell, meaning a special wrinkle or rule is added to the Hunger Games before The Reaping ceremony, in which tribute names are drawn.

The wrinkle of Haymitch’s games was that each district was required to send double the amount of tributes that year, so four competitors from each district doubled the amount of players in the games — making it a whopping 48 versus the normal 24.

For those new to the universe entirely, each District of Panem — there are 12 — is forced to send two tributes each into the Hunger Games, a barbaric tradition that pits these pairs of usually children together in an arena to fight until the death until only one remains. Collins has spoken of the inspiration as gladiator fights and Greek mythology. The two tributes, a boy and a girl, are selected in a Reaping process which involves slips of paper with names on them in a bowl that a Capitol representative pulls from.

In District 12, specifically, where Katniss, Peeta, Haymitch AND Lucy Gray Baird are from, candidates can opt for extra slips of paper with their names on them to get more food or supplies, because the coal-mining district is a poor one.

In a l etter released right before the premiere and release of the film, Suzanne Collins recounted her experience coming up with Haymitch's story.

"The seeds of Haymitch Abernathy's backstory were planted over twenty years ago when I began the original trilogy," she wrote. "In Catching Fire , Katniss and Peeta watch the recap of his Second Quarter Quell games as he silently observes from the shadows. The Capitol had warped the true account and spun reality into vicious propaganda. For Haymitch to tell the truth about what happened would've been too dangerous for his tributes and too traumatic for him."

Will Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson show up in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ?

Yes, the news broke that the original pair who starred in the foundational quartet of films as Katniss and Peeta will be back for the fifth film, a prequel to their story.

Who else is behind the Sunrise on the Reaping film?

Francis Lawrence , who directed The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes as well as Catching Fire and both Mockingjay films, will return to helm this prequel story, penned by Billy Ray , who wrote the script for the first original film's adaptation.

articles.content:
Representing the likes of Megyn Kelly , Tucker Carlson , Chris Cuomo, Justin Baldoni , the Menendez, brothers' family, reality TV stars and Rebel Wilson over the years, Bryan Freedman has never shied away from the direct approach and a bit of controversy in his practice. However, the Hollywood litigator now finds himself accused of "despicable betrayal" in a real thriller.

In the malpractice and fraud complaint filed today in L.A. Superior Court, the Liner Freedman Taitelman + Cooley LLP co-founder is accused of strong arming alleged sexual abuse victims into singing a "hush-money agreement" and playing both sides of molestation allegations against the much accused late Michael Jackson . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News David Ellison Commits To Airing Alex Gibney 'Musk' Doc On HBO Max, Calls Skydance Investor "Greatest Entrepreneur Of Our Time" News 'I Want Your Sex' Sets HBO Max Streaming Release Date

A sequel of sort to the "serial child predator" suit that the now adult the Cascio siblings hit the much litigated (ask Paris Jackson) Jackson estate with earlier this year, today's action paints a portrait of money, star power and fast talking. Represented by attorney Howard King's Avenue of the Stars firm, siblings Edward, Dominic, Marie-Nicole, and Aldo say Freedman exploited "the family’s vulnerability and trust to induce them into signing an unconscionable agreement, which stripped them of valuable legal rights, imposed sweeping confidentiality provisions, and shielded Jackson’s estate and representatives from liability." Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

The usually media available Freedman did not respond tonight to Deadline's request for comment on the sordid accusations. Full Disclosure: In the past, Freedman has been retained by Deadline's parent company PMC to represent them in several legal matters.

In this matter, Freedman first came into the Cascios' orbit about a decade ago in regards to a suit filed by a Jackson fan against members of the family and the Estate's then co-administrator John Branca over a posthumously released album from the superstar, who died in 2009. Later, in the Estate's desire to contain the fallout against Jackson and his legacy from HBO ‘s unsettling and vivid Leaving Nevermind documentary, Freedman is said to have sought the Cascios confidence by advocating for them in an “acquisition and consulting agreement,” that would see the Estate paying each long time Jackson connected sibling $690,000 annually for five years the rights to their life stories. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But it wasn't their life stories the siblings now say the Estate wanted, it was their silence.

“Freedman never explained that this payment was wholly inadequate relative to payments that Jackson and the estate have made to other victims of Jackson’s sexual abuse,” the multiple damages seeking complaint states. “Freedman never explained the agreement’s grossly unfair penalty provision, which requires the entire Cascio family to return all payments if one member discloses Jackson’s crimes to anyone."

Amidst all that, the Cascios assert Freedman was also running a parallel sleight of hand, so to speak.

A"t the time, Freedman represented the Estate, including in connection with litigation against HBO, which had broadcast Leaving Neverland, a documentary about Jackson’s sexual abuse of two other victims, Wade Robson and James Safechuck," they say. "Freedman never told Plaintiffs that the Estate had retained him to silence other Jackson victims from coming forward after Leaving Neverland’s release. Freedman never disclosed to Plaintiffs the conflict created by his representation of the Estate, and he never obtained Plaintiffs’ informed written consent to waive that conflict."

Slipping back into the picture in 2024, Freedman is said to have told the Cascios that the previous deal was “toilet paper” and, having “had enough on the estate,” he was going to fix things for the siblings.

On that occasion, citing Freedman having too many masters, the Cascios went with another lawyer. That attorney informed the Jackson estate that the brothers and their sister "intended to challenge the Agreement as void and unconscionable."

"Branca and the Michael Jackson Company filed an arbitration demand against Plaintiffs, which alleges that Plaintiffs have breached and anticipatorily breached the arbitration, non-disparagement, and confidentiality provisions of the Agreement," today's complaint says, referencing the siblings' other suit of earlier this year.

Responding to that suit this past spring, Jackson estate and its executors attorney Marty Singer called out the Cascios' claims a “desperate money grab.” Pointing out the siblings were so pro-Michael they sat down with Oprah the year after his death to praise him, Singer piled on calling their February 2026 suit a "transparent forum-shopping tactic in their scheme to obtain hundreds of millions of dollars from Michael’s estate and companies.”

"The Estate has successfully compelled arbitration of Edward’s, Dominic’s, Marie-Nicole’s, and Aldo’s federal lawsuit against the Estate, Branca, and other Jackson-related entities in connection with their facilitation of Jackson’s sexual abuse," it adds. "If Freedman had not fraudulently induced Plaintiffs into signing the Agreement, they never would have been dragged into litigation for publicly discussing Jackson’s abuse."

Ordered onto arbitration back in August, that case be heard behind closed doors - but the echos could resonate in the public courts via this latest filing.

In addition to this case, Freedman has over the last year or so been drawn into the pits of PR Dark Arts with the allegations of online smear campaigns, provocative web sites and other underhanded tactics via the Blake Lively vs Justin Baldoni battle and Rebel Wilson taking on her The Deb producers — none of which is a good look by any estimation.

articles.title: Newsmax Fears Fox Freeze-Out on Roku if Merger Is Not Blocked
articles.summary: Newsmax filed an antitrust lawsuit on Thursday that seeks to block the Fox-Roku merger, arguing that the deal gives Fox unlawful monopoly power over the free streaming market. Fox Corp. closed the $22 billion acquisition earlier this month. The Department of Justice cleared the deal the same day, announcing that Fox had made commitments to […]
articles.content:
Newsmax filed an antitrust lawsuit on Thursday that seeks to block the Fox- Roku merger, arguing that the deal gives Fox unlawful monopoly power over the free streaming market.

Fox Corp. closed the $22 billion acquisition earlier this month. The Department of Justice cleared the deal the same day, announcing that Fox had made commitments to keep Roku as an "open and neutral" platform.

But in its lawsuit , Newsmax alleges that those commitments are unenforceable, and raises fears that Fox will deprive it of a key distribution channel. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"No single media company should have the power to determine which news voices Americans can see or hear," said Christopher Ruddy, the CEO of Newsmax, in a statement. "Fox already dominates cable news and has repeatedly sought to undermine Newsmax as a competitor. Now Fox wants to control the very platforms and technology that millions of Americans use to access news and information."

According to the complaint, Fox will control some 70% of the free, ad-supported streaming TV market through its ownership of Roku and Tubi .

"Fox has a long history of anticompetitive animus toward Newsmax," the lawsuit states. "Most notably, Fox has refused to carry Newsmax on Fox’s own free streaming service, Tubi. Now that Fox has acquired Roku – along with (the Roku Channel) – the risk that Fox will further degrade distribution of Newsmax’s content is clear."

The complaint was filed in the Northern District of California.

In response, Fox Corp. noted that regulators have already approved the deal.

“Newsmax’s complaint, which comes after a rigorous review process by regulatory agencies, is wholly without merit," a Fox spokesperson said. "Upon closing, we commenced actively integrating this approved transaction for the benefit of consumers, partners and other stakeholders.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Newsmax filed a separate antitrust suit against Fox last year in federal court in Florida, accusing its rival of using aggressive and illegal negotiating tactics to block it from getting wider cable and satellite distribution. The judge in that case, Aileen Cannon, dismissed it almost immediately as an impermissible "shotgun" pleading.

Newsmax then refiled in Wisconsin, where a judge granted Fox's motion to transfer the case back to Florida. Discovery in the case is on hold pending the outcome of a motion to dismiss.

articles.title: Marvel May Have Revealed Doomsday's Green Witch Two Years Ago, and It's Not Who Everyone Thinks
articles.summary: Marvel Spoilers for VisionQuest follow. Ever since the costumes of Avengers: Doomsday’s so-called “Latverian witches,” were displayed at San Diego Comic Con, Marvel Cinematic Universe fans have been doing detective work to figure out which familiar characters could be under the masks of the mystical villains aiding Latverian dictator Victor von Doom/Doctor Doom (Robert Downey Jr.) […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Spoilers for VisionQuest follow.

Ever since the costumes of Avengers: Doomsday ’s so-called “Latverian witches,” were displayed at San Diego Comic Con, Marvel Cinematic Universe fans have been doing detective work to figure out which familiar characters could be under the masks of the mystical villains aiding Latverian dictator Victor von Doom/Doctor Doom (Robert Downey Jr.) Although none of the color-coded mystery characters, who probably aren’t all actually Latverian, wear her trademark shade of red, many fans assume that the franchise’s first and most popular witch, Wanda Maximoff/The Scarlet Witch (Elizabeth Olsen) will be one of the three. Wanda’s long-awaited return to the franchise in the recent finale of VisionQuest , in which Victor rescues her from her presumed death, initially appears to support this idea.

Some viewers believe Wanda will be revealed as the Doomsday witch in a green costume, specifically, as a nod to a comic book storyline involving her and Victor that Doomsday and next year’s Avengers: Secret Wars , are speculated to be inspired by, in which she wears green. But the fan favorite, mystically-focused, trilogy of series started by WandaVision and concluded by VisionQuest also featured another extremely powerful witch who would make sense in this specific role. Agatha All Along introduced Rio Vidal (Aubrey Plaza), the personification of Death , who is also referred to as the MCU’s original Green Witch. Given this, one can’t ignore the possibility that the 2024 series already revealed her as the Doomsday antagonist, surprisingly directly, before fans even knew the witches would be part of the film.

Rio/Death is introduced as a mysterious former lover of the witch Agatha Harkness (Kathryn Hahn,) who helps Agatha free herself from a spell Wanda used to imprison her at the end of WandaVision . Although she then attempts to kill Agatha, who has already used magic to give herself an unnaturally long life, Agatha convinces her to wait until she can restore her depleted magic powers so their final confrontation can be less one-sided.

Agatha All Along was the first MCU property to explain how different areas and subjects of witchcraft and magic are represented by different colors. After Agatha and the mysterious “Teen” (Joe Locke) assemble a coven to walk the mythical “Witches’ Road,” their peers insist that the group needs a Green Witch to succeed, according to centuries of lore about the Road. It is later explained that, “Green Craft is about the cycle of all living things. Growth and decay in constant flow.” Agatha hastily recruits Sharon Davis (Debra Jo Rupp,) a non-magical civilian for the role, but she is killed during the group’s first magical trial. Rio then appears on the road and replaces her. When the other coven members ask if she is a Green Witch she replies “Less "a" Green Witch and more The Green Witch!” while altering her voice unnaturally. After the rest of the group discovers her true identity, Jennifer “Jen” Kale (Sasheer Zamata) acknowledges that death is part of the cycle of life Green Craft deals with saying that Rio, “Told us who she was from the very beginning.” Rio returning as Doomsday ’s Green Witch would subvert expectations in the same way, presenting her identity in a straightforward manner only for viewers, and possibly other characters, to dismiss her as a suspect precisely because of how obvious a choice she’d be for the role.

Some specific lines from Doomsday ’s trailers can easily be interpreted in favor of this theory. The one that supports it most directly is Erik Lehnsherr/Magneto’s (Sir Ian McKellen) declaration that, “Death comes for us all,” though that is also simply a common phrase that it makes sense to use in a scenario as apocalyptic as Doomsday looks to be. Other trailers feature Victor replying to Thor’s (Chris Hemsworth) threat to send him to Hell by saying, “Hell answers to me, for I am Doom,” while using his own magic powers, which are represented with green light. Some have instead interpreted this as an allusion to Thor’s sister Hela (Cate Blanchett,) the Goddess of Death, possibly returning as one of Doom’s allies, but it could just as easily be a reference to Rio/Death herself.

Death is a long-standing character in Marvel Comics, usually presented as a female, and sometimes referred to as “Lady Death,” or “Mistress Death.” The comic character’s arguably most famous for her role in The Infinity Gauntlet storyline that inspired the Avengers films Infinity War and Endgame . In the comic book arc, Thanos uses the Infinity Gauntlet and Stones to erase half of all life in the universe from existence in the hopes of impressing Death, who he has a romantic obsession with, though it is often ambiguous whether the entity is really communicating with Thanos or if he deludes himself into seeing and speaking with an imaginary version of her. While Josh Brolin’s MCU version of Thanos ultimately had different motivations, the franchise did acknowledge his original portrayal during the character’s introduction. In the mid-credits scene of the original Avengers movie from 2012, Thanos’ servant the Other (Alexis Denisof) advises his master against continuing to wage war on the humans of Earth, saying, “To challenge them is to court death,” which causes Thanos to smile. Given this, some comic fans would probably find it odd to include the Death character in Avengers movies focusing on a villain other than the Mad Titan.

Those who have followed Doomsday ’s production may also question how Death and Doom could come to work together, as they initially seem to have opposite goals. Promotional materials and comments from the cast and crew of Doomsday indicate that Victor will initially pose as an ally to the film’s superheroes, claiming he also wants to stop the collisions between different universes known as incursions. Depending on how closely the film follows the comic book arc its based on this may actually be true, though Victor will inevitably have other, more villainous motives and/or methods that eventually set him against the heroes. One might initially assume that Rio would be in favor of allowing the incursions to continue so that all life in the multiverse is killed. But Agatha All Along emphasized that the character only seeks to ensure deaths deemed necessary by what she sees as the world’s natural order. If she believes the multiverse is supposed to exist and that the incursions and deaths they cause are unnatural she would fight to prevent them. Doom’s line from the trailers about how some specific heroes “have lived stolen lives,” suggests that he will be targeting those whose lives he believes have progressed or been preserved in unnatural ways, which is exactly what Rio does.

Do you think Death is the green witch in Avengers: Doomsday ? Discuss in the comments.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google H.E.R.B.I.E. is getting a brand-new look in Avengers: Doomsday , and this recent update on the movie proves that audiences are going to be divided (at the very least) on this change. Doomsday is just around the corner with a Dec. 18 release date, and of the confirmed characters, the Fantastic Four members are some of the most highly anticipated. For one, the Doomsday trailers already confirmed that the movie is remaining loyal to the comics in that Doctor Doom, Reed Richards, and Sue Storm are going to have a very complicated dynamic that comes with its own baggage and history. However, Sue and Reed aren't the only Fantastic Four members getting audiences excited.

For one, Sue and Reed's son, Franklin, is one of the most powerful characters in Marvel Comics, and The Fantastic Four: First Steps has already confirmed that the MCU is maintaining that too, given that Franklin brought his mother back to life. He will therefore, presumably, be a key character in the fight against Doom. Perhaps slightly less beneficial on that front, but still a very beloved character, the Fantastic Four's robot, H.E.R.B.I.E., will be returning to the big screen in Doomsday , and it was already confirmed that he would be sporting a design change . Now, though, a closer look at Doomsday has made it clear that this really will be a significant change—and it's going to ruffle feathers. Take a look at H.E.R.B.I.E.'s new design below.

When H.E.R.B.I.E. was introduced in the MCU, he featured a very charming 1960s-era style. Given that Doomsday is setting up a multiversal event and it's safe to assume time has passed since First Steps , it was always likely that H.E.R.B.I.E.'s design would be updated at least a little for the new movie. However, this new look at Doomsday has confirmed that this won't be all that minor of a change at all. Instead, H.E.R.B.I.E. is showing off an entirely new look, and it's very likely to cause some controversy within the fanbase, especially for those who loved H.E.R.B.I.E.'s original design (or simply don't want to see major changes for the character in general).

New look at Yelena Belova, Captain America, Reed Richards, Shang-Chi and H.E.R.B.I.E. in ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’ (via @empiremagazine ) pic.twitter.com/vTZBX4o7a8

On the positive side, this new image confirms that Doomsday is going to feature some unexpected but nevertheless perfect team-ups. In this image alone, H.E.R.B.I.E. is walking alongside Yelena Belova, and they will almost certainly be a hilarious pair. This also bodes well regarding the fan concern that Doomsday was going to struggle to bring these various groups together, as Avengers: Infinity War had years and multiple projects to build up to that, and Doomsday will, seemingly, be bringing these universes together with minimal preamble. Hopefully, though, this image is a sign that the groups will mesh just fine. Now, it's just waiting to see how audiences react to this H.E.R.B.I.E. change.

articles.title: Ebenezer Is One of the Best Christmas Carol Adaptations I Have Seen and This Is Why
articles.summary: Courtesy of Paramount Pictures Remakes have always come with the question of "what is the point?" If that is true of films that have been adapted two or three times, then it should be screamed out every time someone mentions the words "new version of A Christmas Carol." As the most adapted fictional work of all time, with almost […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Remakes have always come with the question of "what is the point?" If that is true of films that have been adapted two or three times, then it should be screamed out every time someone mentions the words "new version of A Christmas Carol ." As the most adapted fictional work of all time, with almost 350 adaptations across movies, TV, stage, and more, there can surely be no purpose in retelling the story yet again. Yet despite the well-worn nature of the story, Johnny Depp is currently raking it in at the box office with his movie Ebenezer and I found this to be one of the best versions out there. As one of my favorite books, I have seen a lot of versions of Scrooge's redemption arc played out over the years to compare it to.

Ebenezer is Ti West's version of A Christmas Carol and it is perhaps therefore not surprising to hear that the film leans into some darker moments more than many of the previous adaptations. Along with Depp in the titular role, the cast is fleshed out with brilliant performances from Ian McKellen, Rupert Grint, Angela Riseborough, Tramell Tillman, and others and even brings a few little expansions of the story thanks to West's decision to show and not tell. This includes an opening prelude where Jacob Marley is not dead to begin with, and several other scenes that are described in the story by characters talking about them but are inserted here as full scenes. West also adds in his own extension to the story with an expanded roles for Scrooge's lost love, Belle, the murder of his one-time employer Fezziwig at the hands of a beggar, and even a glimpse into his troubled home-life as a child. That makes this the same story you know, but ever so slightly different at the same time.

When it was announced that Ti West would be directing Ebenezer it was hard to know exactly what audience he would be aiming it at. Having made his name with the X trilogy of horror movies, it would not have been surprising if the movie turned out to be a bloody R-rated affair. Instead, the film is much more than that. It is one of the darkest takes on the source material in terms of its focus on the more gothic elements of Victorian fiction, and being a ghost story at heart, this one does not hold back on delivering some creepy imagery . The ghosts of Jacob Marley, Past, Present, and Yet to Come are joined briefly by the unrestful dead, who beckon and urge Scrooge to save them in moments straight for the horror playbook, but that is only part of the overall tone of the movie.

West's movie sticks to Dickens' story to the point of actually using the novella's chapter titles on screen to break up the story into segments. The gloom and grimness of the era is almost palpable as the camera sweeps around the streets of London, showing off its grimy beggars, dirty windows, and hopeless society. Throw in some misty scenes, graveyards of haunted spirits, and a morbid moment of Ebenezer coming face to face with the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come's true identity in one of several real moments of eerie horror. Although some movies have tinkered in this area, there have been very few that have really treat the story for what it is, and that is something that sets West's version apart from many of its peers.

Naturally, the make or break aspect of any adaptation of A Christmas Carol comes down to the man (or in some cases woman) playing the role of the miser turned good egg leading the movie. Over the years some of the greatest actors have embodied the role of Ebenezer Scrooge, from Michael Caine and Patrick Stewart to George C. Scott, Bill Murray in the contemporary Scrooged , and even Ryan Reynolds in Apple TV musical movie Spirited . Now, it is Johnny Depp's turn and he does not let the opportunity to fully embrace the role with all his heart. And just like some of the best actors, the aforementioned Caine among them, Depp is most at home when he is playing it as the same character he plays in many of his movies, and there is nothing wrong with this as it brings something to the role that no other actor can. He cackles and gibbers his way through some scenes, always with the greatest amount of expression on his prosthetic-covered face.

I have watched so many versions of A Christmas Carol that the story itself is one that brings no surprises. What that means is all it can do is use different visual tricks and slight nuances that can only be brought about by the vision of a director and the actors that bring the characters to life. Among the many versions told over the years, many will agree that the 1984 movie starring George C. Scott and 1992's The Muppet Christmas Carol are right up there as two of the best adaptations. Ebenezer cannot touch these, but for me it comes in not too far behind. What is interesting now is whether another new dark take on the story can come along and take its place very soon, with Robert Eggers set to follow up the success of Nosferatu and this year's upcoming Werewulf with his own Christmas Carol . Only time will tell on that score, but for now, Ti West and Johnny Depp's version is the most unique and memorable made this century.

How does Ebenezer stack up against other versions of A Christmas Carol for you? Let us know in the comments.

articles.summary: While there has been a lot of shakeup and uncertainty when it comes to the future of the DCU with the announcement last week of James Gunn and Peter Safran’s departure from DC Studios there is one thing that has remained unchanged and it’s that Man of Tomorrow is one of 2027’s most anticipated movies. Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google While there has been a lot of shakeup and uncertainty when it comes to the future of the DCU with the announcement last week of James Gunn and Peter Safran’s departure from DC Studios there is one thing that has remained unchanged and it’s that Man of Tomorrow is one of 2027’s most anticipated movies. Even with what comes after still a bit of a question mark , fans are eager to see the follow up to last year’s Superman . Now, it seems that those in attendance at a Warner Bros./Skydance presentation today got a look at footage from the film — including an exciting new suit for Superman.

According to various reports on social media, during a presentation today, clips from Man of Tomorrow were screened for those in attendance. The exclusive footage reportedly featured David Corenswet’s superman in new super suits, including a white suit that some are saying is inspired by comics, specifically All-Star Superman . The footage also has people speculating that a proper trailer or teaser for the film, which comes out next July, will be released soon.

When it began circulating that the footage shown at the WB/Skydance event featured a white super suit for Superman, many immediately started making a connection to the iconic comic book story, All-Star Superman from Grant Morrison and Frank Quitely and for good reason. Yes, All-Star Superman is widely considered to be one of the best Superman stories ever told, but it is also a comic that has been connected to Gunn’s take on the Man of Steel from the start. Before 2025’s Superman was, well, simply Superman , the film was called Superman: Legacy and in that iteration, Gunn explained that it wasn’t an origin story but one that focused on an established hero trying to balance his Kryptonian heritage with his human upbringing — a story that All-Star Superman tells better than any other.

And, ultimately, the story we got in the 2025 film did balance the heritage and the upbringing and deliver the sort of Superman story Gunn promised he would. But it also wasn’t a direct adaptation of All-Star Superman . Instead, that book was just one of several that Gunn drew from to shape his story. Given that we already know that All-Star Superman is, in a sense, a part of the DCU DNA, a new, white suit could be another way to bring the comics into the story without being a direct adaptation. If it is a nod to the comics, there could also be a purpose for said white suit. In the comics, the white suit is designed specifically to convert other light frequencies to the energy of a yellow sun, letting the hero take on a particularly difficult foe.

Of course, there could also be another reason for a white super suit: a nod to Superman’s Kryptonian heritage as white has already been established as the color Kryptonians dominantly wear.

All we know is we want to see that suit for ourselves. Are you hopeful we get a teaser or a trailer soon? Sound off in the comments or on the forum!

articles.title: The Time Robert Pattinson Snuck Around Rikers Island (and Why It Could Help Him With James Bond)
articles.summary: Among the actor’s colorful roles is one rather surreal real-life moment in the hoosegow.
articles.content: Amid all the talk of whether Robert Pattinson ’s experiences will allow him to pull off a convincing James Bond , none feel as instructive as the time he went to prison. It was the middle of 2016, and Pattison didn’t commit any crimes, but he badly wanted to be seen as a someone who did. Pattinson was preparing for his role as Connie Nikas, a con on the run, in the Safdie Bros. jangly fugitive-drama Good Time . The Safdies knew some incarcerated people at Rikers, including their friend Buddy Duress, who would go on to be in the film. So, as Pattinson told a reporter writing about the movie in 2017, he begged Josh to get him into the facility. The director obliged, and while inside he and the future James Bond "just kind of went everywhere; we didn’t really ask for permission,” as Pattinson recalled at the time. (The interview was part of a story centered on walking around colorful parts of Queens with the Safdies, a tale in its own right.) The pair got deep inside the infamously locked-down institution, talking to wardens and inmates alike about life on the inside. One interaction in particular stuck with Pattinson. "I had gotten into all this makeup because I didn't want anyone I met in there to find out who I was or what I was doing; I wanted them to think I belonged. And I thought I was convincing. And then one of the inmates said to me, ‘What are you doing in here? Is it for a scared-straight program?' [The program to influence innocent-adrift teenagers.] I wasn’t convincing anyone." "I thought I was looking like some kind of tough guy but he could see right through me," he continued. (Pattinson is known for telling tall tales in interviews but this one is true — Josh Safdie confirmed the account.) On the one hand this unpersuasive cosplay can seem like one more reason the actor makes for an ill-fitting James Bond — you generally want your 007 to be a little more weathered than a pretty teenager, even ten years later (and also may validate all the skeptics who don’t like that this was kind of a corporate decision .) On the other hand, what’s more James Bond than sneaking around Rikers and getting out unscathed? A general MI6-ish resourcefulness marked Pattinson's time working with the Safdies. Hot off his Twilight run, Pattinson had reached out to the erstwhile collaborating brothers brothers simply after seeing a promotional photo for Daddy Longlegs , their gritty semi-autobiographical coming of age movie. He then read their script for what would become Uncut Gems and begged to be in that. The Safdies didn’t see Pattison in any of the top roles, including the lead middle-aged hustler played by Adam Sandler. But the filmmakers were so intrigued by his persistence that they decided to write a whole chase-drama for him — the movie that became Good Time . Sweet-talking your way into the confidence of a pair of powerful people so they'll do something for you they weren’t otherwise ready to do? M would be proud.
